mechanism:
%load-wallet-records calls (bl.rpc:parse-descriptor desc-str network :require-checksum t) on the stored string (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1068) with no handler around it, so whatever the descriptor parser signals is what loadwallet answers -- an address/key-level bl.rpc:rpc-error at +rpc-invalid-address-or-key+ (-5) whose text is descriptor.cpp's own ("Invalid characters in payload", "Provided checksum '%s' does not match computed checksum '%s'"; ours reproduces those strings verbatim, src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:98-101). Worse, the value codec itself is unguarded: wdb-parse-descriptor-value on a TRUNCATED record runs its byte-reader off the end and signals SB-INT:INVALID-ARRAY-INDEX-ERROR, which is not an rpc-error at all and so leaves through the generic branch of handle-single-request (src/rpc/server.lisp:407-420) as -32603 "Internal error: Invalid index 153 for (SIMPLE-ARRAY (UNSIGNED-BYTE 8) (153))...". Core funnels every one of these through one classifier. WalletDescriptor's SERIALIZE_METHODS calls DeserializeDescriptor, which runs Parse(str, keys, error, /*require_checksum=*/true) and throws std::ios_base::failure("Invalid descriptor: " + error) for ANY parse failure -- checksum mismatch, invalid characters, unknown function alike (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletutil.h:41-64; ToString writes the checksum, descriptor.cpp:153/942-959, so the stored string always has one). LoadDescriptorWalletRecords catches ios_base::failure and returns DBErrors::UNKNOWN_DESCRIPTOR with the wallet-level text "Error: Unrecognized descriptor found in wallet %s. " plus either "The wallet might have been created on a newer version. " or "The database might be corrupted or the software version is not compatible with one of your wallet descriptors. " (chosen by the VERSION record's last_client) plus "Please try running the latest software version" and the details (walletdb.cpp:764-784). LoadWallet returns early on UNKNOWN_DESCRIPTOR before the ACTIVE*SPK records can turn it into a misleading corruption error (walletdb.cpp:1141-1147), wallet.cpp:2400-2404 turns the class into the user-facing "Unrecognized descriptor found. Loading wallet %s

The wallet might have been created on a newer version.
Please try running the latest software version.
", LoadExisting returns nullptr at wallet.cpp:3140-3144, LoadWalletInternal prefixes "Wallet loading failed. " and sets FAILED_LOAD (wallet.cpp:286-291), and HandleWalletError's default branch answers RPC_WALLET_ERROR (-4).
consequence: An operator whose wallet was written by a newer build, or whose descriptor row is damaged, is told an address or key is malformed (-5) instead of being told the wallet holds a descriptor this software does not recognize and may be too new -- and if the damage is a truncation rather than a bit flip, is told the node had an internal error (-32603) with an SBCL array-index report. Both codes are wrong: Core answers -4 with a wallet-level sentence in every one of these cases. The wallet refuses to load either way, so nothing is mis-loaded and no wrong value is acted on: S3, diagnostic class. No wallet_*.py asserts these strings (Core's own coverage of the class is wallet_migration/unit-level), so the divergence is invisible to the functional suite.

(c) value truncated by 6 bytes -- Core's ios_base::failure case -> reply (-32603 "Internal error: Invalid index 153 for (SIMPLE-ARRAY (UNSIGNED-BYTE 8) (153)), should be a non-negative integer below 153."). (d) the descriptor string replaced by an unknown function xx(<pubkey>) carrying a deliberately wrong checksum -> (-5, checksum mismatch, because the checksum is checked before the function name). Core at d3056bc: wallet/walletutil.h:41-64, wallet/walletdb.cpp:764-784 and :1141-1147, wallet/wallet.cpp:2400-2404 and :286-291, wallet/rpc/util.cpp:127-157, script/descriptor.cpp:121-124, :153, :942-959, :2857-2862.
fix_shape: Reproduce Core's classifier at the walletdescriptor branch rather than fixing one message. Wrap both the value decode (wdb-parse-descriptor-value) and the parse-descriptor call at src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1068 in one handler that catches any condition -- rpc-error, byte-reader bounds errors, and anything else -- and re-signals bl.rpc:rpc-error at +rpc-wallet-error+ (-4) with Core's exact text: "Unrecognized descriptor found. Loading wallet <file>", a blank line, then "The wallet might have been created on a newer version." and "Please try running the latest software version.", keeping the original condition's report in the debug log the way Core appends "\nDetails: %s" to strErr. Once the VERSION record is actually read (finding b314f13a), pick between Core's two middle sentences using last_client > our client version, which is the reason Core threads last_client into LoadDescriptorWalletRecords at all. Abort the load at that point, as Core's early return does, so no later record can produce a second, more confusing message. A regression test should cover all three shapes -- bit flip, non-charset byte, truncated value -- because they take three different paths in the current code and only one of them is a descriptor-parser error.
